newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki rebounds strongly on forestries and Nokia.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki rebounds strongly on forestries and Nokia.

text.p: Shares staged a sharp rebound on Tuesday and ended at new record levels as Nokia erased Monday's losses and forestries continued to rise on improving prospects, brokers said.

Forest industry shares gained two percent in early dealings and added another 1.20 percent after UPM-Kymmene and Metsa-Serla announced a restructuring of their joint pulpmill company Metsa-Botnia and Metsa-Serla's acquisition of UPM's folding boxboard mill.
"In the short run, this had a positive impact which showed up in prices. It brought buyers to the market," said one broker.
UPM's and Metsa-Serla's deals gave UPM a 700 million markka profit and some brokers said this helped make UPM the most attractive forestry stock.
"For UPM the news was clearly good (and) I think forestry buying will increasingly centre around UPM," said one.
UPM closed 3.70 markka higher at 97.70, up almost four percent, and trade was an active 66 million markka. Metsa-Serla advanced three percent to close at 35.00, up one markka.
Nokia closed up 9.30 at 268.00 markka -- two markka above its close last Thursday, before Fed chairman Greenspan's comments sent shockwaves around markets on Friday.
